READABILITY.evidence: Type names are clear and consistent (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookie, CookieAttribute), every exported field has a doc comment, and the CRD descriptions are generated. consistent_hash.go itself was not visible in the diff, so this is judged from the API and wiring.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: a separate consistent_hash.go, plus wiring in constructor.go, the plugin and mergeConsistentHash (merge.go L625-663). Deepcopy and CRD come from codegen. I could not see the helper bodies, so sharing of dedup/sort between build and merge is unconfirmed.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: CEL rule for disable exclusivity, MinLength=1 on key fields, and Validate is wired. TTL is a free-form string with no CRD pattern, so bad durations are only caught at runtime. I could not inspect the regex/TTL error handling.

C7-09-CASE1.evidence: Golden /merge route: rule-policy entries come before route-policy entries (X-Shared, x-rule, x-route), duplicates are removed, output is re-sorted headers→cookies→queryParameter→filterState, and the metadata 'merge.TrafficPolicy...consistentHash' lists both policies. Hidden tests pass.

C7-09-CASE2.evidence: Golden: an empty policy yields 'connectionProperties: sourceIp: true'. The /disable route has no hashPolicy even though the route-level policy sets one. The CEL rule 'when disable is true, no other fields may be set' is in the types and the generated CRD, and tests cover it.
